title: Design a Rate Limiter
prompt: Design a rate limiter that can be applied in front of an API to limit each client to a configurable number of requests per time window, working correctly across multiple servers.
requirements: Functional: allow/reject requests based on a per-client rate limit rule, support different limits per API/client tier
Non-functional: must work correctly with multiple application servers behind a load balancer, minimal added latency, should not become a single point of failure
discussion_points: Algorithm choice: token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window counter, sliding window log/counter
Where state lives so multiple servers see a consistent view (e.g. a shared fast store)
Race conditions when many requests arrive concurrently for the same client
What happens if the shared store is briefly unavailable — fail open or fail closed?
How this scales as the number of distinct clients grows very large
